newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus says Alenia, Saab keen on jumbo project.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says Alenia, Saab keen on jumbo project.

text.p: European plane consortium Airbus confirmed on Wednesday that Italian manufacturer Alenia and Sweden's Saab were interested in investing in its $8 billion project to build a 555-seat superjumbo.
An Airbus spokeswoman told Reuters that Alenia had not signed an agreement, but that "they have expressed interest. Saab has also expressed its interest very strongly recently."

The Wall Street Journal Europe reported on Wednesday that Airbus' A3XX superjumbo project director Juergen Thomas said Alenia planned to take a 10 percent stake and Sweden's Saab was close to signing an agreement to take up to five percent.
Thomas told the Journal in an interview that a Korean consortium had expressed interest and his "personal guess" was that they would take between five and 10 percent.
Korean officials from Samsung, Daewoo, Korean Air and Hyundai visited Airbus's Toulouse headquarters last month to discuss the project.
Airbus is also reviewing the antitrust implications of a planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp of the United States, the spokeswoman confirmed.
"We are looking at the long-term implications. For the time being, I can't comment further," she said.

Thomas said he believed Boeing's recent scepticism about the project reflected dissatisfaction with its own 747-stretch design rather than insufficient market demand. He said he expected Boeing to return to that segment of the market.
Airbus expects the project to cost $8 billion. "That is the target figure for development costs," the spokeswoman said.

Around 33 percent of the financing is expected to come from launch aid from European governments, 40 percent from risk-sharing partners in Europe and Asia, and the rest from the Airbus consortium partners, Aerospatiale of France, Daimler-Benz, British Aerospace Plc and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
Airbus aims to formally launch the superjumbo plane in December 1998 for delivery in 2003.
